title: Etale path between geometric points
statement: Let $Y$ be a connected scheme and let $\bar y$ and $\bar z$ be geometric points of $Y$ in the sense of [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $F_{\bar y}$ and $F_{\bar z}$ for the fibre functors on finite etale covers of $Y$ from [def-galois-fibre-functor]. An etale path from $\bar y$ to $\bar z$ means a natural isomorphism $\gamma:F_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\bar z}$: for each finite etale cover $P\to Y$ it specifies a bijection $\gamma_P:|P_{\bar y}|\xrightarrow{\sim}|P_{\bar z}|$, commuting with the maps of fibres induced by every morphism of covers.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take C = the finite etale covers of Y, D = FintypeCat, F = F_ybar and G = F_zbar, already supplied by def-galois-fibre-functor; an etale path is the type F ≅ G (CategoryTheory.Iso, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Iso.lean:53). The natural transformations have precisely the component and naturality fields in CategoryTheory.NatTrans (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/NatTrans.lean:53). CategoryTheory.Iso.app (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/NatIso.lean:53) extracts each component isomorphism, FintypeCat.equivEquivIso (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/FintypeCat.lean:130) identifies it with a bijection, and CategoryTheory.NatIso.ofComponents (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/NatIso.lean:181) packages the family of bijections and the stated naturality equation back into F ≅ G. No Galois-category axioms or path-existence theorem is used.
